title: Brief your designer
recap: Pipo wrote Priya a clear brief for your launch banner.
funFact: A good brief saves a round of back-and-forth. Agents can write one in seconds, as long as you give them the details. Next, Pipo orders the shipping boxes, and spends your money!
postcard: a glowing laptop in a dark creative studio showing Pipo's email about a deep green and gold launch banner: {body}
situation: We need a launch banner! Should I email Priya, your designer, about it?
facts: 🎨 Priya at Kiln Studio, for the $150 you agreed on
📐 Two sizes: a shop page banner and a square Instagram post
🌲 Brand colors: deep green and gold
systemPrompt: You are Pipo, a friendly personal assistant for the founder of a small online business. You can send emails for them. You do what they ask: if they ask you to send something, you send it; if they ask to see it first, you write a draft and wait for their OK.

tools.name: send_email
tools.description: Send the email right away. Use this when the user wants it sent.

tools.name: draft_email
tools.description: Write the email and show it to the user without sending it, so they can check it first. Use this when the user wants to read it before it goes out.

to.description: Who gets the email: a person, an email address or a mailing list

subject.description: The subject line, up to 8 words

body.description: The email text, up to 55 words

lines.text: Draft ready, waiting for your OK to send

slots.label: What do you want Pipo to do?

pieces.label: Email Priya at Kiln Studio to book the launch banner
pieces.text: Email Priya at Kiln Studio, the freelance designer I work with. Ask her to design the banner for our launch.

pieces.label: Email the designer about the banner
pieces.text: Email the designer about the banner.

pieces.label: Two sizes: shop banner and square Instagram post
pieces.text: We need two sizes: a wide banner for the shop page and a square Instagram post.

pieces.label: I need it by Tuesday, December 1
pieces.text: We need it by Tuesday, December 1.

pieces.label: The $150 we agreed on
pieces.text: Confirm the $150 price we agreed on.

pieces.label: Make it pop, she gets the vibe
pieces.text: Tell her to make it pop, she gets the vibe.
pieces.tip: "Make it pop" means something different to everyone. Sizes, dates and price are what a designer can work from.

pieces.label: Our colors: deep green and gold
pieces.text: Our brand colors are deep green and gold.

pieces.label: Whatever looks trendy right now
pieces.text: Use whatever looks trendy right now.
pieces.tip: Trends change every week. Your own colors make the banner look like your brand.

pieces.label: Show me the email first
pieces.text: Show me the email before you send it.

pieces.label: Send it right away, Priya's quick
pieces.text: Send it right away, Priya's quick.

flaws.hint: "The designer" doesn't say who to email.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know you meant Priya at Kiln Studio, so the email isn't going to her.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo which sizes you need.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know about the two sizes, so Priya would have to guess.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo when you need it.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know about Tuesday, December 1, so Priya doesn't know there's a deadline.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo the price you agreed on.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't mention the $150 you agreed on, so the price is left open.

flaws.hint: "Whatever looks trendy right now" doesn't give Pipo your brand colors.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know your colors are deep green and gold, so the banner might not look like Ember & Oak.

flaws.hint: Asking to see the email first lets you fix it before Priya reads it.
flaws.explain: Pipo sent it straight away, so you never got to check it.

lesson: A good brief says who it's for, what you need, by when and for how much. Then check it before it goes.
